warnings: To make this clear I explain a typical trading day here. You wake up and check all standard, lazy and quick currencies to find possible trading opportunities (such a check normally takes about 30 minutes). In this check you will face one of the three possible situations. 1- You may find one or two trading opportunities, so you place your trades. 2- You do not find any tradable opportunity at all, so you leave your trading station and come back a few hours later to check again. 3- You find some forming trading opportunities but that is not the time to trade yet, so you estimate the best trading time (according to the trade parameters), leave your computer and then come back in the specific time to trade. Working with ten major and minor currencies this way, you should normally find 2-4 trading opportunities each day.

A. In 50% of the times (whatever the actual and forecast figures are), the relevant currency pair do not significantly react to the news (mostly low or medium impact and seldom high impact news) at all (except for low range hysteric moves during the first minutes) and the price takes its main course respecting the dynamics of the price (trends, patterns and price rejections).

In news trading, you have accepted an inevitable loss of 25% beforehand. In other words, according to the historical data, 25% of the moves will be against you and your stop loss will be definitely hit. So, in theory, your risk/reward ratio (see chapter 21) will be 25:75 or 1:3 but in reality it will be worse because we do not expect that all the 75% of our favored trades end up to a good profit (hit our profit target). Regarding these facts we need to maintain a risk/reward ratio of 1:2 or better to compensate the 25% of inevitable stop loss hits and other possible premature exits.
During the time, as you trade according to the high performance system, you will find that all the trading opportunities do not perform equal.
